A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
global FCFS and the relative distribution of load are two important factors to take into account in the design and analysis of two-class queueing systems with two dedicated servers.
global FCFS and the relative distribution of load over customer classes are important design parameters for multi-class multi-server systems.
global FCFS is a good policy for a system with two customer classes if the relative load distribution is such that the load on one class is significantly larger than on the other one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global FCFS principle may lead to a substantial increase in the customer delay, as compared to a system without global FCSF.
, in multi-class multi-server systems, a global FCFS policy may not be beneficial, and may even deteriorate the system performance.
the global FCFS queueing policy may be a viable alternative to individual queues in multi-class multi-server systems, as long as the load is distributed in a proper way.
